# `liber:camera@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:camera` package (`camera.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem cameras - bounded formats, explicitly started capture into buffers the CLIENT owns, and honest timing and loss.  THREE PARTIES. An ordinary client holds `camera`: it lists cameras and reads their formats, and has no operation that starts anything or reaches a frame. A client PermissionManager granted capture holds a `camera-capture` connection minted through the private `camera-admin` for ONE camera and the life of one launched component; it negotiates, registers its own buffers and starts explicitly. A PROVIDER - the USB Video class module, or the in-guest fixture - serves `liber:camera-device@1`, and CameraService is its one consumer.  THE CLIENT OWNS THE MEMORY. Frames are written into memory objects the client created and keeps paying for; the service holds handles and metadata only, and allocates no frame storage on a client's behalf. A completed buffer is LEASED to the client until it gives that exact lease back; nothing overwrites it meanwhile, and when no buffer is queued a new frame is dropped and counted, never queued without bound.  TIME IS WHAT WAS MEASURED. Every frame carries the host time it was assembled at, in the boot's monotonic nanoseconds; the device's own clock rides beside it only when the device gave one, as raw ticks with its width, its frequency when known, its domain and its reset generation - never converted, never subtracted from a clock it is not correlated with.

## Types

### resource `frame-buffer`

A memory object the CLIENT created, for the camera to fill.  `@kernel(memory-object)` is what makes the `@rights` guard on `register` refuse a handle of any other kernel object rather than checking rights on whatever it was handed.

An opaque kernel object, transferred as `handle<frame-buffer>`.

A camera as this service knows it: DeviceManager's publication identity and the incarnation of the service that issued the handle. A replaced camera is another camera, and a new authority decision.

## Interfaces

### interface `camera`

INVENTORY: cameras and their formats. No capture, no buffer, no start.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `cameras` | `cameras() -> result<list<camera-info>, error>` |  |
| 2 | `sizes` | `sizes(camera: camera-id, generation: u64, format: u8, offset: u8) -> result<format-page, error>` |  |

### interface `camera-capture`

CAPTURE on the one camera this connection was minted for, for as long as its owner lives. Nothing starts until `start`; renegotiating needs `stop` first, and a stopped stream is retired - a new one registers its own buffers.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `camera` | `camera() -> result<camera-info, error>` |  |
| 2 | `sizes` | `sizes(generation: u64, format: u8, offset: u8) -> result<format-page, error>` |  |
| 3 | `negotiate` | `negotiate(request: stream-request) -> result<negotiated, error>` |  |
| 4 | `register` | `register(buffer: handle<frame-buffer>) -> result<u8, error>` | At most four buffers, each at most 8 MB and 32 MB in all; the same backing once per stream. |
| 5 | `start` | `start() -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 6 | `events` | `events() -> stream<capture-event>` |  |
| 7 | `release` | `release(buffer: u8, lease: u64) -> result<unit, error>` | Give back exactly the lease a frame carried; the buffer is queued for the camera again. |
| 8 | `stop` | `stop() -> result<unit, error>` | Answered once the camera has returned every buffer it held. |
| 9 | `status` | `status() -> result<capture-status, error>` |  |

### interface `camera-admin`

THE MINTING ENDPOINT, PermissionManager's alone. The alias names a camera the service's configuration binds to provider metadata, and resolves to exactly one current publication or the mint fails.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `mint` | `mint(alias: string, owner: handle<task>) -> result<capture-grant, error>` |  |
| 2 | `revoke` | `revoke(camera: camera-id) -> result<u32, error>` | Revoke every capture grant on one camera: their streams stop as a closed connection's would, and a client has to be granted again. Answers how many grants ended. |
